name: Traffic Grey B
lede: Traffic Grey B is a dark, slightly green grey from the German RAL road-and-signage standard, the darker half of a matched pair with Traffic Grey A.

sections.title: The darker half
sections.body:
RAL, founded in 1927, lists this hue as RAL 7043, a screen approximation of that spec [1]. It pairs with the lighter [[traffic-grey-a]], the two meant to work together in road markings and signage [1]. The books consulted do not explain why RAL split the traffic greys into two letters rather than two separate names, so that choice stays undocumented [1].

Its nearest named neighbor in our library is [[dark-neutral-grey]], close enough to be mistaken for it on screen [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive finds this hue, as photographed, in 615 of 23,781 paintings (2.59 percent), more common than 77 percent of the named colors we track [2]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 55 of 1,674 paintings, at 2.1 times the expected rate for paintings from that century [2]. Inside a painting it most often plays a mid-tone, in 40 percent of its 326 occurrences [2].

[[painter:henri-matisse|Henri Matisse]] is its most devoted painter here, carrying it in 9 of 50 of his works, 6.7 times his home museums' baseline [2]. The earliest matching painting is dated 1099, 828 years before RAL recorded the standard in 1927, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. It shares canvases more than chance with [[nickel]] and [[deep-gull-grey]] [2].
